contracts.rule: A node in a generation graph is addressed by its key, the chain of ids from the root (`3/7` for node 7 inside instance 3), never by its id alone. The hashes, the journal, the executor's targets, the cost walk and every `gengraph.*` command's `node` prop use it.
contracts.prevents: A node inside a group instance sharing its id with a root node, since every graph's ids start at zero, so the two would share a hash, a journal record or a command target.
contracts.detail: A root node's key is its id, so keys in a graph with no groups are unchanged and a journal written before groups existed still matches its nodes. Every `node` prop on a `gengraph.*` command resolves through `resolveNodeKey`, so the pane writes an instance's override as `gengraph.setProp` on `<instance>/<id>`, and the agent's whole-graph rewrite keeps an instance under `group: <ref>`.

contracts.rule: An edit inside a group instance can only override a value; `decideGenEdit` refuses a structural edit there with the sentence `structuralEditsRefused` gives. Structural edits go to the group's definition, written as `vngen/work/graphs/lib/<ref>.json`.
contracts.prevents: One instance's wiring silently diverging from the definition every other instance shares, so editing the definition no longer describes what that instance runs.
contracts.detail: Every `gengraph.*` editing command reaches a definition through its `group` prop. The renderer only reads the definition file; it never writes it.

contracts.rule: Renaming a node type's socket or prop needs a migration in the same commit: bump the type's `typeVersion` and add a `NodeMigration` step that lands on it. `migrateGraphJSON` replays the renames over a file's JSON before `readGraphFile` deserializes it.
contracts.prevents: A file written before the rename loading with the old key as an orphaned socket, its link reaching nothing visible and the renamed key at its default, so the wiring is lost silently and the changed hash redraws the slot.
contracts.detail: path.ux reconciles a loaded node against its definition by key. The replay moves sockets, props, links, a group's forwarded rows, and the `{name}` tokens a template embeds, which puts the node back on the hash a freshly created one would have. `registerGenNode` refuses a migration whose targets name nothing on the class or whose last step stops short of the declared `typeVersion`. A file keeps its old keys until something writes it back, so a migration stays in place rather than being deleted a release later.

contracts.rule: A concept image never gets a node in the task graph: `generateConcept` records a hash of the request (prompt, params, refs) as the asset's `sourceTask`, and nothing a run plans consumes the asset, so a project holding a concept plans exactly the tasks it planned before.
contracts.prevents: A concept bound to `{locationId: 'cafe'}` being taken for that location's plate, or a sketch the author asked for changing what the next run plans and pays for.
contracts.detail: The asset is bound to what it sketches so the document tree and the backlink panel can find it. Every binding lookup outside the document tree filters by `kind` first, and the planner resolves a shot's plate by task hash rather than by manifest binding.

contracts.rule: A shot's task inputs carry its location twice: `buildShotPrompt` names the location, and the plate's asset hash leads `refs`. So rewriting a scene's heading re-keys every shot in the scene, unlike retyping a line, which re-keys nothing.
contracts.prevents: Treating a heading edit as free, like other prose edits, when the next run re-renders every shot in the scene; the price has to be shown before the edit runs.
contracts.detail: The planner passes the plate first in `upstream`, then each subject's portrait and outfit sheet. A heading edit inverts the rule that prose edits are reported as drift rather than re-rendered, so the price counts these shots as `restaged`, never as `drifted` (`script.headingRestagesShots`, in `@vn/scriptedit`).

contracts.rule: A shot in a staging-sheet group carries `params.extra.sheet`, a hash of the sheet's prompt, its reference hashes in order and the group seed, so anything the sheet is drawn from re-keys every member at once. A shot in no group carries no `extra`.
contracts.prevents: A member drawn from an old sheet while the others are cut from a new one, or a sheet change that re-renders nothing, because the sheet's inputs are not in any member's identity.
contracts.detail: What re-keys the members: the members and their order, each member's framing, cast and camera, the plate, and the group's notes and seed. A shot outside a group carries no `extra`, so no hash that predates the field moved. The seeds are derived from the project and the manifest, never from a task graph, by `sheetSeeds`, which the planner, the scheduled runner and `gengraph.run` all call; a group's seed and notes live in the shots file and reach the model scene's `sheets` through `readAllShots`. A sheet is rerolled by changing its seed (`story.setSheetGroup`), never by force: `gengraph.run` refuses `force` on a graph where a node feeds more than one output (`sharedAncestors`), because a forced run to one output would redraw the sheet for it alone and leave the other members' frames cut from the old one with nothing to re-key them. Every slot a graph binds shares its one journal and its one `Graph` object in a process, and `runBoundGraph` serialises the runs of one graph, because seeds are written onto the graph's own sockets: two members running at once would read each other's prompt and references, and the sheet would be drawn once per member rather than once per group.

contracts.rule: Outside the scheduler, a `done` record is written only by adoption (`@vn/artgen/adopt`). The maintenance writers re-write a record the log already held, verbatim, or write `pending`.
contracts.prevents: Marking a task done with bytes no run produced for its current inputs, so the next run skips it and the slot's picture no longer matches the project.
contracts.detail: `vn/element-types` lets only the scheduler and `@vn/artgen/adopt` import `@vn/taskgraph/write`, and a test refuses any other file passing `tasksLog` to `appendJsonl`. `adopt` hashes the inputs it is handed, derived from the project as it stands, so it can only mark done the node whose output these bytes now are. Its callers live in `adoptslot.ts`: `adoptSlot` (an author hands bytes to a slot), `fileGraphDraw` (the picture an interactive graph run ended on, `via: graph`), `holdPortrait` (an older portrait draft the gate approves, `via: restore`, so `repairCurrent` does not hand the slot back to the logged output) and `repinAdoption` (the desktop repin keeping its bytes). Adoption is refused for a `portrait:` slot (the gate owns it), for mock-marked bytes, and for superseding a render that already holds the slot without an explicit `replace`. `promoteConcept` is one caller of adoption. In `@vn/taskgraph/maintain`, `restoreDone` and `logRestored` append a copy of a record a tombstone replaced, and `logTombstone` and `logRequeue` write `pending`.

contracts.rule: A batch decomposition writes a storyboard only for a reachable scene with no `work/shots/<sceneId>.json`, has no `force`, and never writes a baseline: a scene the model does not answer for is named and skipped. Hosts refuse mock or unresolved keys by name.
contracts.prevents: One bad key permanently baselining a whole project, because an absent file is the only signal meaning "decompose this scene", and re-decomposing a kept scene changing its shot ids and so re-rendering art already paid for.
contracts.detail: Once written, the shots file takes precedence permanently. A hand-placed first shot (`story.newShot`, the agent's `edit_scene op=newShot`, `write_storyboard`) writes the file and so ends decomposition for that scene just as permanently. `decomposeScene` returns a `source` and a `reason` rather than throwing so that this batch can tell a baseline from a model answer; inside one run a single silent fallback is `providers.textFallback` holding. `keepBaseline` exists for a caller that wants the deterministic storyboard, and nothing in the app passes it. `vngen decompose --mock` and the desktop command refuse mock providers by name.

contracts.rule: Authored `artNotes` are appended to what a builder derived, entity note first and the narrower rung second, and an empty note adds nothing, so a project that authors no notes composes byte-identical prompts. A shot's prompt reads only the shot's own notes.
contracts.prevents: Re-keying every task in every project that authors no notes, and losing the style preamble, reference scaffolding and closing frame clause that keep a picture on-model, which a replaced prompt would drop.
contracts.detail: `artNotes` is an optional free-text field at five rungs: `Character`, `Location`, `Shot`, each `Outfit` and each `LocationVariant`. Setting a note costs money by design, like an outfit and unlike a scene edit: the note is in the prompt, so it re-keys exactly the tasks its rung reaches. `buildShotPrompt` leaves out the entity notes because they already reach the frame through the plates and sheets it references. The test worth having is the byte-identical output of a project with no notes, not the feature. Where the notes, seeds and image models are written is `prompts.artRungsShared`, in `@vn/artgen`.

contracts.rule: Art notes, image seeds and image models are authored at the same five rungs, addressed as `character:<id>[/<outfit>]`, `location:<id>[/<variant>]` or `shot:<sceneId>/<shotId>`, and every host writes them through one parser and one write path, with the same refusals.
contracts.prevents: Two hosts drifting into two rung vocabularies, so the agent and the desktop refuse or write the same authorial act differently, or create the outfit, variant or shot a typo named.
contracts.detail: An entity rung is written into the sheet the model was built from, through `@vn/model`'s `apply*Edit`; a shot rung into `work/shots/<sceneId>.json`. An empty value clears the rung back to inheriting. The narrowest seed wins (`seedFor`) and is in the task hash; the narrowest image model wins (`modelFor`) and is outside it, and a slot a generation graph binds takes the graph node's own model and seed instead. The Wiki pane's sheet form is a second writer of the same keys (`art_notes`, `seed`, `image_model`) through `@vn/parse`'s front-matter codec, because the `art.*` commands re-serialise the whole front matter and lose the author's comments; the model reads the keys back identically, and a blank box removes the key. `regenerate_asset` is always confirm-gated and refuses where the host has no pipeline (vnauthor). The agent reads a rendered picture back through `view_image` (`describeAsset`, a plain vision question rather than the P7 reviewer).

contracts.rule: P5 receives the scene as identified lines, `[<lineId>] <kind>/<speaker>: <text>`, never as flattened prose, and a decomposition that binds none of the scene's real line ids falls back to the baseline.
contracts.prevents: A model copying an empty `"coversLines":[]` from the response template, which produces shots that are drawn and never displayed, because the exporter shows a shot only where its lines are.
contracts.detail: The system prompt asks the model to assign every line to exactly one shot, in order; the code does not enforce that, and a line the answer leaves uncovered stays uncovered. What the code enforces: line ids the scene does not have are dropped, a decomposition that binds no real line falls back to the baseline (`withCoverage`), and an uncovered first line goes to the first shot, so a scene cannot open on a blank frame. `coversLines` is not in a frame's task inputs, so these repairs re-key nothing.

contracts.rule: The reference graph over slots stays acyclic: `prompt.addRef` runs `refCycle` in its check and refuses a reference that would close a loop, naming the whole path. The cycle is over slots, not hashes.
contracts.prevents: Tasks that are never ready, because each waits on the other, so a run appears to do nothing and reports no error.
contracts.detail: Hashes cannot cycle, but bindings can: "Aiko's portrait references Aiko's gala sheet" closes a loop although no hash repeats, because the sheet's prompt already references the portrait. A ref cycle is invisible to `topoOrder`, which reads `Task.deps`. Left unchecked, `doneOutput` answers `undefined`, the shot is skipped, and the plan-run-replan loop starves in silence. `firstCycle` finds a loop already on disk in a hand-edited project, and the planner calls it so such a project fails loudly.

contracts.rule: The P7 reviewer sees only what `shotSpec` says about the shot: its own framing, location and cast, with the prose of its covered lines marked as context only. `spec.characters` decides who must be in frame, and an empty list means an absence is not a defect.
contracts.prevents: A reviewer handed the scene synopsis flagging every shot, plates included, for characters the scene mentions but the shot never ordered, so the refine loop spends every attempt and lands on `needs_human`.
contracts.detail: `Shot.castOptional` exempts a shot that has a cast from the same trap: the subjects stay on the shot, so their sheets still reach the generator as references, but `shotSpec` hands the reviewer an empty `characters` and the description says an absence is not a defect. Without it, a frame the reviewer will never accept (a figure seen from behind, a crowd, a hand) spends the whole cap. `story.requireCast` writes the field, normally from the Shot Coverage strip. `shotSpec`'s output never enters a task's `inputs`, and `castOptional` is read only by `shotSpec`, so neither re-keys the shot: setting the field changes what the next review asks and does not by itself redraw the frame.

contracts.rule: The text steps (P1 location enrichment, P5 shot decomposition) call the LLM with structured-output enforcement and fall back to a deterministic baseline when the step fails, so a whole run completes with mock providers and no API calls.
contracts.prevents: A run that stops at the first text step a mock, missing or failing model cannot answer, which would make the pipeline impossible to run end to end without paid calls.
contracts.detail: P5's baseline is one establishing shot carrying the scene's cast plus one medium shot per character, each on the location's first variant. The establishing shot carries the cast because it covers the narration and action beats, which describe the characters doing things; a scene with no cast gets a bare plate. `decomposeScene` never throws: a failure becomes a `baseline` decomposition with a `reason`, so a caller that persists can refuse to write it (`planning.storyboardOnRequest`). P1 keeps the mined location when enrichment fails. Changing the baseline changes the prompt and re-keys establishing tasks, but shots are persisted, so an existing project keeps its old decomposition until `vngen/work/shots/*.json` is deleted or edited.

contracts.rule: A character or set-location is a file whose front matter says `type: character` or `type: location`, found only in `characters/<id>/character.md`, `locations/<id>.md` and `wiki/**/*.md`, and it is read and written only in the file it was found in.
contracts.prevents: Approving or editing a `characters/<id>/character.md` rebuilt from the id, which silently writes a file that is not the one loaded, and treating every stray Markdown file in the wiki as an input.
contracts.detail: In the two conventional directories the tag is implied by the directory and may be stated redundantly; stating the other kind there is an `entity_tag_conflict` error rather than an override, because a document changes kind only when its file moves. In the wiki a file is an entity only if it carries the tag, and an untagged file belongs to the story bible and is skipped without a diagnostic. Discovery yields an `EntityDoc` (`id`, `file`, parsed `doc`, raw `text`), and `entityFile(docs, id)` is how `vngen approve`, the desktop session, testkit and `vnauthor`'s edit tools find their target. When two files claim one id, discovery warns `duplicate_entity` naming both and prefers the conventional file, then the lexicographically first path. Unparseable front matter is an `entity_file` diagnostic rather than a thrown load: an error under the conventional directories, a warning under the wiki. That the declared `id:` agrees with the file's name is `script.entityIdMatchesFile`, checked by the model build.

contracts.rule: A character or location sheet's front-matter `id:` must equal the id its file's name implies (the directory for a character sheet, the filename stem elsewhere); a mismatch is an `entity_id_mismatch` error and the entity is dropped.
contracts.prevents: A sheet such as `characters/ada/` declaring `id: ren`, which produces a character no file on disk names, so every path derived from the id points somewhere the entity is not.
contracts.detail: The disagreement is reported and never resolved by picking one side, the way `sceneFromDoc` treats a scene whose filename and `scene:` key disagree. Discovery itself is `script.entityByTag`, in `@vn/store`.

contracts.rule: Editing a scene's heading through `setHeading` moves no line id and no coverage, restages every shot in the scene onto the new heading's variant, and counts those shots as `restaged`, never as `drifted`, in the price shown before the edit runs.
contracts.prevents: A shot whose stored `Shot.location` names a variant the new location does not declare, which the planner skips silently and permanently, and an edit that re-renders art being reported as harmless drift.
contracts.detail: The heading is not a `SceneLine` but `location` + `locationVariant` + `headingPrefix`, which `headingOf` reassembles and `parseHeading` reads back. Restaging goes through the `relocated` channel on `LineOp`: `Shot.location` is a variant id persisted in `work/shots/<sceneId>.json`, and the planner's `locationTask(…, shot.location, …)` skips a shot whose variant the location does not declare. Why a heading edit re-renders is `identity.headingRekeysShots`. The prose still describes the old place; the op's message says so and names the agent. `story.setHeading` is not `confirm: true`, because a confirm command is never checked, and the check is what raises the warning.

contracts.rule: Line ids are allocated and stored, and a read never writes: a new line takes its id from its scene's allocator, never from its position, and loading a project allocates ids in memory only.
contracts.prevents: Re-pointing every shot below an inserted line at a different line, which re-renders that art at cost and reports nothing.
contracts.detail: `Shot.coversLines` binds art to `<sceneId>:L<n>`, so an id derived from position would re-point every shot below an inserted line. `splitScenes` prefers a `[[line: L4]]` note (a Fountain note leading the element it names) and allocates only for unmarked elements, starting from the scene's `[[nextline: 12]]` mark raised past every id in use; a stale allocator is a bug and never justifies reusing an id. Duplicate and dangling marks are `error` diagnostics. Allocation happens in memory, and loading a project never allocates. The `story.assignLineIds` command (undoable, over `assignLineIds` in `packages/model/src/lineids.ts`) persists the ids: it adds only whole marker lines, re-parses its own output, and discards the patch unless the re-parse reproduces the same scenes line for line, because a note inserted above a `CHARACTER` cue would turn that cue into action and the lines below it would no longer parse as dialogue.

contracts.rule: `outfitFor` alone resolves what a subject wears, in order: the shot subject's own `outfit`, then the scene's `[[outfit: id=outfit]]` marker, then the character's `default_outfit`. An absent field defers to the next level.
contracts.prevents: The prompt builders, the planner and the desktop resolving an outfit in different orders, so a shot is drawn in one outfit while its reference sheet, or the surface describing it, names another.
contracts.detail: A `ShotSubject` with no `outfit` inherits, which is why `deterministicShots` and the decomposer emit shots without one. `ResolvedOutfit.origin` names the level that answered, so a surface can say which rather than "inherited". `outfitText` falls back to the outfit id when nothing describes the outfit, so a wardrobe can be named before it is described and an undescribed project keeps its prompts. An outfit edit re-renders, unlike other scene edits: the outfit is in `buildShotPrompt`, so a change re-keys exactly the shots it reaches. The sheet fan-out follows from the same function: `usedOutfits` is the character's default plus every scene marker and shot override over reachable scenes, which is `outfitFor`'s range, so a character no reachable scene casts plans no sheets and a shot cannot depend on a sheet nothing planned. A subject out of its default takes that outfit's front sheet as a reference (a frame needs the clothes, not a turnaround), which reaches the planner a wave later, the way a shot waits on its plate.

contracts.rule: A scene edit that spans several chunk files is computed and proved in full before any file is written, and an existing chunk keeps its front-matter block byte for byte; only the body is rewritten.
contracts.prevents: A splice refused on the third file leaving the first two already changed, and a re-serialized YAML block silently dropping the comments the author wrote in it.
contracts.detail: Deciding is split from writing for both write paths: `planMarkerEdit` and `planSceneEdit` touch nothing, so a command's `check` and its `run` ask the same function, and the apply step writes a plan that already proved itself. The front-matter block is spliced back from `splitFrontMatter`'s prefix rather than re-serialized.

contracts.rule: A scene is one `scenes/<id>.md` file whose front matter is `scene: <id>` and nothing else and whose body is one complete Fountain scene with its own heading. The id comes from the filename and the front matter, and the body cannot override it.
contracts.prevents: Renaming a scene by editing its prose, and a key such as `next` or `location` stated both in front matter and in the body, so an edit written to one is read from the other.
contracts.detail: The front-matter schema is closed, so a key the body owns is a `scene_frontmatter` error; a filename and `scene:` key that disagree are `scene_id`; a body with no heading or with two is `scene_body`. A `[[scene:]]` marker in a chunk is ignored with a warning. A directory has no document order, so `start:` in `project.yaml` names the entry scene rather than whichever file sorts first. Which files hold scenes, and what a writer patches, is `script.sceneSourcesOneLoad` in `@vn/scriptedit`.

contracts.rule: Writing a scene to Fountain and parsing it back returns the same scene, `parse(write(scene)) ≡ scene`, for every field the model carries except `shots`. `sceneToFountain` writes from `Scene.lines` and the heading fields.
contracts.prevents: A prose edit that re-serializes a scene silently changing it, such as turning `EXT. ROOFTOP - NIGHT` into `INT. ROOFTOP - DAY`, which also changes the location variant the plate is drawn from.
contracts.detail: It is the scene counterpart of `fromDoc(toDoc(x)) ≡ x` for characters and locations, and a property test over the `@vn/testkit` scripts and hand-built scenes pins it. `Scene.body` was removed because flattened prose cannot be split back into its parts: `NAME:` and an action paragraph containing a colon are the same string. The model keeps what Fountain says, including the heading's prefix, its time-of-day variant and `transition`/`lyric`/`centered` lines; `section`, `page_break` and dual dialogue are dropped deliberately. Blank lines are structural: a `[[…]]` marker line is not blank, so a cue always gets a blank line above it, nothing but a `[[line:]]` mark goes between a cue and its first dialogue line, and anything that could be read as another element is written in its forced form (`!`, `@`, `>`, `~`). `needsForcedAction` tests every alternative reading the parser has. Byte-exactness is not a goal: the surgical patchers (`branchpatch.ts`, `lineids.ts`) still handle files the author wrote, because their formatting is the author's.

contracts.rule: `loadInputs` alone decides which files hold scenes, reading only `scenes/<id>.md`, and every scene writer patches the sources `sourcesOf` derives from the same `LoadedInputs` the model was built from, never from a second look at `scenes/`.
contracts.prevents: A model built from one file while an edit is written to another, or a writer patching whatever is on disk by the time it writes rather than the bytes the model was read from.
contracts.detail: Nothing reads the older `screenplay/*.fountain` form, so a model can no longer be built from one file while edits are written to another. A project holding a screenplay and no `scenes/` gets a `legacy_screenplay` error naming `vngen import`; a screenplay left beside chunks gets a `stray_screenplay` warning to delete or rename it. `loadInputs` (`packages/store/src/worktree.ts`) also decides which file is the leftover, through `findScreenplay`, which the importer calls too, so the file the reader complains about is the file the importer converts. What a chunk may contain is `script.sceneOneFile`.

contracts.rule: A shot has no position field: its place is where its covered lines sit. Moving a shot moves the block of lines it covers, through the scene write path, and only a contiguous shot can move; one with another shot drawing inside its lines is refused by name.
contracts.prevents: A second ordering kept beside the prose that can disagree with it, and a move that silently interleaves shots or re-renders art.
contracts.detail: The exporter's `sceneBeats` emits a `show` beat whenever the covering shot changes down `scene.lines`, so nothing needs renumbering. Coverage is a set and interleaving is normal (the deterministic decomposer gives the establishing shot every narration line while each medium shot takes one character's dialogue); a shot with holes is on screen in more than one place, so it has no single position to move from. A move changes no hash: ids stay the same, coverage stays the same, and every shot's covered lines keep their relative order, so `proseHash`, which walks `scene.lines` in order, does not drift and nothing re-renders.

contracts.rule: Each asset root writes its manifest through one queue: a write waits for the previous one, re-reads the file, and applies only the rows its own instance changed.
contracts.prevents: Two parallel tasks renaming onto `manifest.json` at once, which fails on Windows (EPERM), and a stale instance writing back rows another instance removed.

contracts.rule: Image bytes are stored once per root under their content hash: base art (portraits, model sheets, plates, concepts, references) in `assets/`, shot frames in `vngen/build/`. A write routes by `AssetKind` alone, and each root has its own manifest.
contracts.prevents: A base subtree that is its own git repo losing its provenance to the project's manifest, or one picture stored twice under two names, so a reader cannot tell which root an asset lives in.
contracts.detail: Base art lives at `assets/objects/<hash>.<ext>`, frames at `vngen/build/assets/<hash>.<ext>`. Reads consult both roots, which is safe because a hash names the same bytes wherever it is. A hash both roots hold is a picture adopted across them, and the project row answers when it is a frame (`rowRoot`). A project written before the split still resolves, because its base art stays indexed in the project manifest. Writing a base kind while the base root is `unavailable` throws rather than writing there.
